title: Burst capacity synthesizer for interactive spikes — proportional GPU headroom across weights/KV/activations
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Interactive tails (short, high-QPS bursts) cause sudden KV and activation pressure that leads to tail latency spikes or evictions of hot weights on multi-tenant GPUs. Our current static headroom buckets are either too conservative (wasted capacity) or too aggressive (evictions under microbursts).

Goal: Design and implement a Burst Capacity Synthesizer (BCS) that creates a proportional ephemeral headroom fabric across weights, KV cache, and activations to safely absorb interactive spikes while minimizing steady-state waste. The synthesizer should integrate with continuous batching and the memory ledger so decisions are reversible and observable.

Approach summary:
- Build an Ephemeral Reserve Ledger (ERL) that tracks transient "burst tokens" per tenant at 1s resolution. Tokens are funded by forecasted slack and reclaimed automatically.
- Compute proportional reserves across three compartments: weights (pinned slots for model shards), KV (cache pages / prefix trees), activations (dynamic slab windows). The proportionality is derived from recent footprint ratios and a per-tenant SLA weight.
- Admission smoothing: integrate with the batching admission filter so that when ERL is depleted, new requests are throttled to the background queue or routed to quantized model variants.
- KV cold-window prefetch: on detected spike start, prefetch likely KV prefixes with a conservative budget (configurable via feature flags) to reduce cold-start misses while preserving headroom.
acceptance_criteria: A1: ERL exposes per-tenant burst tokens and a taxonomy (weights, kv, activations) to the Console and is queryable from telemetry (prometheus label 'erl_tokens').
A2: Under the synthetic microburst workload (see design doc), 95th percentile completion latency reduces by >=30% compared to baseline without BCS with <=10% increase in steady-state memory usage.
A3: When ERL is evicted, admission smoothing reroutes >=95% of affected requests to fallback variants or queues them for <250ms additional latency, preventing weight eviction.
A4: Implementation has unit/integration tests and a canary rollout plan with runtime-1.21 feature flag 'bcs-enabled'.
comments: 2025-11-18 - Ava Chen: Created ticket. Initial design doc attached. Shared simulation spikes that motivated the work (customer support incident INC-2025-11-12).

2025-11-19 - Mateo Alvarez: Ran micro-sim locally. Observed that a 2s 10x QPS spike causes KV thrash and weight eviction when headroom <12% on A100-like node. Pushing a prototype ERL data model and a simple allocator in branch 'feature/bcs-proto'.

2025-11-20 - Priya Nair (review): Questioned proportional split defaults — suggested startup defaults of (weights:40, kv:35, activations:25) and a simple decay to recent footprint over 60s. Asked for trade-offs on weight pinning vs. eviction grace periods.

2025-11-21 - Mateo Alvarez: Updated proto: added micro-slab compaction hook and an activation transient compression (ATC) mode that opportunistically compresses recent activations to free short-term headroom. Performance numbers: ATC adds ~3ms to hot-path for 10-15% memory reduction in activations on our benchmark.

2025-11-22 - Engineering Sync: Agreed to expose two knobs in Console: 'burst_token_rate' and 'kv_prefetch_budget_ms'. Security/infra flagged the need for K8s resource limits to be validated before canary rollout.

2025-11-24 - QA (Elena R.): Wrote integration test harness that replays production traces with injected microbursts. Found a race: ERL reclaim path sometimes double-counts tokens when a request is retried. Filed ENG-276101 as follow-up dependency.

2025-11-26 - Mateo Alvarez: Opened PR for ERL core + admission smoothing: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123. Benchmark run attached in PR shows 35% reduction in 95th tail under synthetic spike. Preparing canary run in us-west-2 cluster.

2025-11-27 - Product (Samir Patel): Requested an observable metric for 'eviction-avoidance-score' to show business impact (reduced model reloads and lower customer latency incidents). Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-11-28 - Mateo Alvarez: Fixed token double-count race (ENG-276101 merged). Updated canary checklist and added rolling abort conditions if memory usage increases >15% or weight eviction rate increases. Next: canary rollout in staging on 2025-11-30.
